summary: Former Franklin County, PA lookout. The register dates the wood tower to 1905 and says it is no longer standing. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot wood tower; the register calls it a tree tower
facts.status_note: The register says the tower is no longer standing. No source we read describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Register gives 1905 as the build year
Register says the tower was still used circa 1917

evidence.supports: built 1905, still used circa 1917, no longer standing; described as a tree tower
evidence.quote: This tree tower was built in 1905, still used circa 1917, and is no longer standing.
<1918: A 30-foot wood tower erected prior to 1918. (Report of the Department of Forestry, December 31, 1917)

evidence.supports: regional article: a state forest observation tower in Franklin County in 1905; does not name Oak Knob
evidence.quote: followed by a state forest fire observation tower in Franklin County in 1905.

evidence.supports: hiking directory lists an Oak Knob Trail
directions given to Mont Alto State Park

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls it a tree tower; the Forest Lookouts page calls it a 30-foot wood tower. The two pages use different words, and the story reports both.

sources.title: The Lumber Heritage Region, North West and North Central Pennsylvania
Oak Knob Trail, Franklin County Pennsylvania Hiking Trails

notes_for_editor: Thin record: a register page, a Forest Lookouts page with one line on the tower, a regional article that does not name Oak Knob, and a hiking directory that does not mention a tower. Two searches found no removal date, staffing or fire history, and the register gives no coordinates. A search result named a peak called Oak Knob in Quincy Township near Mont Alto; I could not confirm it is the tower site, so the story does not use it. The trail directory is a 2000-2014 listing. The story is short by design.
